reviews.comment: Ehh not the best. Is not great with his time and lectures are not to the point like they should be for physics 1. Did not cover stuff on time. if u get him just watch videos of Tatiana Erikhimova on classroom physics to learn.

Great guy. Cares for his students. Wants you to succeed. Provides opportunities to go over your test with him in office hours. He lowered the bounds for what counts as a passing grade. Downside is his lectures are very disengaging. He tends to ramble on subjects which causes one to loose interest. Take him if you can self teach.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: i'm a pretty average engr student. he's super nice. not great at conveying the material. I learned pretty much nothing from lectures. I think he forgets he's speaking to a room full of 18 year olds and not issac newton himself. if you're a robot you'll do great but if ur like a 3.0 kinda student, learn from recitations and vids, you'll do alright.
Struggles to explain things and often goes on unnecessary tangents. Lectures are very unengaging.  Fries cares a lot and is a sweet man, but is rough as a lecturer. Take Dr. Erukhimova if possible.

He's very nice and understanding, and is respectful to students unlike some of the other physics staff. His in class examples help a lot and he answers lots of questions in class and will go back and explain something again if you don't understand it during the lecture. He does hour long reviews a few days before common exams which helps a lot.

He is a sweet guy but I REALLY tired to learn in his class. However, he was not a good explainer, and spent majority of time talking about unnecessary information or  just made it confusing. You have to learn the concepts outside of class/recitation. Did curve final, and is very accessible. Avoid him, unless you've already taken AP PHYS

I think doctor Fries is a very underrated professor. His lectures weren't the best but he always cared a lot. He always offered to go over exams afterwards and would often give back points if he could. His final exam was very fair and felt very reasonable and supposedly gave a generous curve on top of that. The class itself is hard but he is fair.

Lectures were the most unengaging I've ever seen, literally made me fall asleep. Didn't feel like I learned much from his lectures - only from recitations. After exam 2 I started watching nodurfts lectures which seemed much better structured. Sweet man, but not good at getting students not interested in physics to enjoy it. Only got A bc of curve.

I wish that I could rate the difficulty as a 10/5. This was the hardest class that I have ever taken in my entire life. Lectures are meh. The reason why I rate him so high is that he is accessible in office hours, will go over exams (in class and in private), has review sessions before all exams, curved very generously, and has a fair final exam.

I would have gotten an A in this class, but I had health issues. He is very understanding, and you can tell he wants you to succeed. Read the textbook and do the practice problems, and you should be fine.

lectures are slow and very easy to fall asleep in. He spends the same amount of time on the difficult ideas as he does on the basics. He goes through practice problems on the slides but other profs do it better. I learned everything from going through problems in recitations.

If you are not able to get into the other Don't Panic sections, I highly recommend taking Fries (even as your first choice). His lectures are on more on the slow side, but he has plenty of examples and explanations of concepts. Dr. Fries is happy to go over exams with students for feedback, and he has super helpful exam review sessions. Take Fries!

Great professor, really thorough when it comes to answering questions in class. The slides he creates could be a little more concise and quicker. overall a good prof for understanding mechanics and helping when you need it. Also has some great handwriting.

The course itself is standardized and hard no matter what, not his fault. I did not like that he would get off-topic during lecture then try to squeeze in remaining material at the very end forcing you to stay a few minutes after sometimes. He does not make eye contact with the students during lecture and looks at the wall. Bad speaker, good proff
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 206 is a hard class, but Fries does everything to help make it easy. He is very accessible outside of class, especially after tests, and is very good about communicating what is on the tests and what you should know.

I attended lectures of all the 206 Don't Panic profs, so I can compare.  Not best, but a solid 3rd choice. Fries has Good English, Great handwriting, posts slides, his mic is set at a nice level.  Sometimes uses Latin (like "a priori").  Slides have more theory than others, but he does enough nice sample problems.  Exam zoom reviews are useful.

Fries is an easy grader and gives a lot of good example problems in class. He does lecture *super* slow though. If you're new to the content it's great, but everyone got a little sleepy sitting through those hour and 15 min lectures.

Professor Fries is an amazing lecturer. I was worried that I would find my professor's lectures boring, but I was always attentive and found it easy to pay attention in class. He gave many opportunities for exam reviews outside of class time which was very generous and helped with my grades and overall preparedness for exams.

Fries is a funny and caring guy, but the course 206 is just challenging. Don't panic; it is so test-heavy that you have to constantly review for the next exam weeks in advance. Fries tends just to read off the slides but for the most part its pretty helpful. He does a few examples to prepare, but I felt like more could be done. He could be worse
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think Dr.Fries is a very intelligent man and is extremely passionate about teaching physics, however I do think the entire structure of this course limits the abilities of the professors that teach this style of the course. As an extremely math-based course, I felt like it should have focused more on math.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fries was a good professor and made it clear that we would be graded almost solely on our exams. His lectures felt like reviews of topics or overviews rather than teaching new material. Reading the book is an absolute must. Overall was a nice and enthusiastic professor but could have taught better.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a really nice professor who cares about his students' learning. With some supplemental material such as the textbook and Don't Panic supplemental resource site, you have the materials needed to perform well. I would recommend the SI sections if you are having trouble understanding exam problems. Overall good lectures and materials.

Fries is a good prof to take for 206, not sure why his rating is so low. The grade in the class is based almost entirely off exams, but hes very generous with exam review and partial credit. Lectures can sometimes be dull, but if you stay focused youll be fine.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Fries is an extremely intelligent man, however, he does not explain lectures very well. I did most of my learning outside of lectures. I only showed up for poll questions which counted for a grade. He holds review sessions and really does care about your success. If Tatiana or Dawson isn't available, Fries is the man.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Fries is a really nice person! Although he does not showcase a lot of examples in class and sometimes starts a new chapter 5 minutes before the end of class, you can still ask him to solve problems during office hours. He also does review sessions where he will go through prior exam problems in order to help prepare students for exams.

Prof Fries brought a lot of energy to lecture and it is not hard to see that he is very smart and passionate about physics. That being said, the lectures were average, and I did most of my real learning at the recitations. Lectures were where he would explain concepts, but I already knew the concepts from high school so I didn't learn much.

Dr. Fries is an average professor. He's a fine lecturer that isn't particularly interesting or difficult. He's obviously very smart and sometimes tries to teach 218/206 on a much higher level. His exam averages were consistently 10 points lower than the other Don't Panic sections, but its still easy to get an A.

PHYS 218 is a very challenging no matter who teaches it, so you will have to do a lot of work to get a good grade. Exams are 4 questions 25pts/Q and you have 1-hour to complete it, so it is very easy to mess up.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He tries his best to make the material understandable, but it doesn't help when he jumps from chapter to chapter without finishing up. There is online homework and pre-lecture quizzes through ecampus almost every week so the book is very necessary. I honestly recommend taking Don't Panic over University Physics any day of the week.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Fries isn't particularly good or bad. You will learn more on your own through the book, but he is willing to bump your tests by a few points if you feel like you got scuffed (it will happen). You are probably better off taking another 218 DP prof. If you are stuck in his class, go to Tatiana's review sessions they are the only reason I passed.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: ABSOLUTE WORSE. I took him for Don't Panic, and every test, he had the lowest average by at least 7 points. He told us he hadn't taught in three years (its 2018 rn), and he has no idea how to teach Don't Panic effectively. Completely depended on A Plus Tutoring (DO GO THAT IF YOU STRUGGLE). Avoid him at all costs.

NO. just no. Going to lectures made it worse. He doesn't know how to break things down at all which makes everything ridiculously confusing. He's obviously passionate, just sucks at explaining everything. He also jumps around a lot in lectures and takes forever to explain one chapter. Super nice guy, good intentions, but AWFUL prof.

You need to have a good background in calculus to do well.  I didn't read the book, but I know those who did, did better than me  THIS IS "DON'T PANIC" PHYS218!  I think the material is just difficult overall, he does his best to convey the concepts and is extremely passionate.  I heard he writes the tests and Erukhimova approves it.

Dr. Fries is a great guy! He tries very hard to make the lectures interesting, and always answers questions mid lecture about content. He cares very much about his students' grades, and quickly responds to emails during the day. I highly recommend Dr. Fries.

Dr. Fries serves to make an already difficult topic even more difficult and confusing. His notes that he posts online are semi-helpful. He does clicker questions in class so attendance is basically mandatory. His lectures are clouded by a lot of fluff and not enough examples and "need to knows" for the tests. NO CURVE. Take another prof if you can!

Fries goes into his own world when he lectures. The things he covers are usually just the theories but never goes over examples of what the tests are like. He makes the simplest of things like antiderivatives sound complicated. A-plus tutoring helped a lot though. The help-desk can be semi-helpful too, but I prefer tutoring.

This prof is super sweet but he often doesn't understand that you're trying to get points back on a test when you go to talk to him, so just be blunt. Otherwise, this is a hard class in general and his notes are super helpful.
